class_guess: Bell eats counter: binary counter on 2-cell digits (10 = 1, 00 = 0) with junk separators, bitten once per bell
summary: Each bounce adds 1 to a binary counter and moves 3 bell cells to a middle field; each bell end eats a counter digit.
mechanism: Turn config R(u,e) = 0^inf u <C 0 1^e 0^inf, u = w 1 (101)^k (w counter, 1 separator, (101)^k middle field). Bounce: R(w 1 (101)^k, e+3) -> R(inc(w) 1 (101)^(k+1), e) in 6k+4t+9 steps (t = trailing 1-digits); exact on all 60,001 turns to 5.1e7.

Eat (e = r in {0,2}): z = inc(inc(w)); z = p 00 -> R(p 1, 3k+3+3[r=2]); z = q c 10 -> R(q 101, 3k+2+3[r=2]). Matches all 631 checked real eats (287 from A, 344 from the certified start B). So e mod 3 is always 0 or 2.

Start B (IndBECv1 cert) stays on the clean orbit R(enc(s) 1, 3s) -> R(enc(s+1) 1, 3s+3). Start A keeps leaving it: odd eats make 010 tails and lone-1 separators inside w (90 of 289 cycle starts to 5e7 are not clean); inc passes through separators; w never contains 1111, which every halting inc input up to length 13 but one has. 88 and 280 run the same orbit (identical tape at 1e9): 280's table equals 88's with state B split by entry; they diverge only if 88's F reads 0 or 88's B (entered by D1) reads 1, which are exactly the two halting reads.

history.skeleton: cycle start R(w 1 (101)^k, e) after an eat (k = 0 or 1)

rules.name: R1 bounce (clean counter)
rules.cases: v>=1, k>=0, e>=0; enc(v) = v in binary, digit 1 = 10, digit 0 = 00; t = trailing 1-digits of v (overflow included); cross-checked with tools/sim.py on 20 more

rules.name: R2 inc through a 110 separator
rules.cases: enc_d = d digits with leading 00s; the separator is transparent to the carry

rules.name: R3 inc through a lone 1 then 00
rules.cases: b < 2^(d-1) (top digit 00); when the top digit becomes 10 the word is R2's form

rules.name: R4 eat, clean counter
rules.to: 0^inf w' <C 0 1^e' 0^inf, w' by the parity of v (see cases)

rules.name: R5 eat, any counter word
rules.cases: r in {0,2}, k>=1; random words from the run; also exact on all 631 real eats (A and B)

rules.name: R6 inc does not depend on k, e
rules.cases: 2,000 distinct counter words from the run; random k, e pairs give the same inc(w)

rules.name: R7 certified orbit (start B)
rules.cases: s>=2; s bounces (R1) then one even eat (R4)

template.diff: same table, start B (its A..F = our B,C,A,E,D,F; no mirror); our start A = its C
template.note: Cert = hlin with side_binary_inc_rule d1=[0;1] (our names: l 00 (10)^n <C 0 r -> l 10 (00)^n 0 F> r), i.e. R1 on clean words; its orbit is R7 and uses only R4's even case. Ours also needs odd eats (e = 2 mod 3 cycles), separators (R2, R3) and the generic eat R5; 7 hlinx configs already fail on start A.

strategy: Find one regular language L of counter words w (clean digits, lone-1 separators, 010 tail) closed under inc (R1-R3, R6) and the eat (R5), with e = 0 or 2 mod 3; halting needs an inc on words with 1111-type runs, which L must exclude. Then a hand proof (Rocq: inc lemmas per word shape + progress_nonhalt_cond), with 280 covered by the shared orbit.
risks: No closed language yet: separators are born at odd eats and die when eaten (29 junk-eat shapes in 83 junk eats); an 8-gram closure (words <= 20) reaches halting words after 3 rounds.
inc on general words is known only operationally (R1-R3 cover clean and single-separator words; multi-separator words rest on sampling, R6).
280 halts on different reads (B after D1 reading 1); a shared proof must exclude both 88's and 280's halting reads.

checkpoint_questions.text: cyclestarts_A_vs_B: are there orange/maroon (junk) cells near the counter's right end in the left panel (start A) and none in the right panel (certified start B)?
every300_3e5: do the white triangles (bells) get steadily taller down the picture, with no sudden collapse?
Next stage: spend up to 2 h on an automaton search for a closed counter-word language (then a hand proof), or park? Recommendation: language search.

stats.growth: span ~ t^(1/3) (3,420 cells at 1e9, 7,346 at 1e10; bell grows ~3 cells per cycle, cycle cost ~ bell^2)

status_reason: Mechanism pinned: every turn to 5.1e7 is a bounce (R1/R6) or an eat (R5); the certified start B is the clean orbit R7. Ours leaves the clean words (junk separators from odd eats), and no closed invariant language is known yet.
